# Vienna 1683 – Medicine & hygiene

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from eras/europe-1683-vienna.yaml — do not edit -->

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Contagion by invisible living agents (germ theory)** [`contagion_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/contagion_theory.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. Sorbait recognised an infection in 1678 and was not believed. Plague rules treat goods and people as catching, yet bad air and God's wrath remain the stated causes. Local: Paul de Sorbait; Pest-Ordnung (1680, Sorbait's revision of Mannagetta's ordinance); Kircher's Scrutinium pestis (Rome 1658) in Jesuit libraries. Elsewhere: Delft: Leeuwenhoek sees animalcules but links none to disease.
- **Abandoning bloodletting, purging and mercury (end of humoral medicine)** [`bloodletting_harm`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bloodletting_harm.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Physicians prescribe bleeding, purges and emetics, also for plague and dysentery patients; barber-surgeons carry it out. Van Helmont's printed attack on bleeding is read as Paracelsian polemic. Local: medical faculty of the university; Bader and Wundärzte (barber-surgeons).
- **Counting and mapping cases to find causes (epidemiology)** [`epidemiology_mapping`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/epidemiology_mapping.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The city records deaths with a cause after inspection of each corpse, but nobody tabulates them by street, well or parish. Local: Totenbeschauprotokolle (death-inspection registers); parish burial registers. Elsewhere: London: Graunt's Observations on the Bills of Mortality (1662).
- **Hand washing with soap** [`hand_hygiene`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/hand_hygiene.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Washing hands is table manners. Surgeons, Feldschere and midwives go from one patient to the next without washing; soap and lye are at hand.
- **Boiling drinking water and protecting wells** [`boiled_water`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/boiled_water.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Wine and beer are the daily drink. Water comes mostly from house wells sunk near cesspits. The Ottomans cut a suburban conduit on 18 July; firewood runs short. Local: house wells (Hausbrunnen); Hernalser Wasserleitung (1565); Siebenbrunner Hofwasserleitung (1553) to the Hofburg; fountain on the Neuer Markt.
- **Slow sand filtration and chlorination of town water** [`water_filtration_chlorination`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/water_filtration_chlorination.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. A sand filter bed is ordinary masonry and gravel work, but nobody sees a reason for it. Chlorination is out of reach.
- **Latrines and sewers (keeping excrement out of water, food and soil)** [`sanitation_sewerage`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sanitation_sewerage.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Old drains (Mörungen) and cesspits empty into the Danube arm, the Wien, the Als and the Ottakringer Bach; no network. In the siege refuse and carcasses stay inside the walls. Local: Unterkammeramt (maintains the Mörungen); cesspits (Senkgruben) in house yards.
- **Food hygiene (cooking, flies, carriers)** [`food_hygiene`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/food_hygiene.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept low. Spoiled meat is judged by smell and market inspection. Flies and cooks' hands are not suspected; the Ruhr is blamed on bad air, unripe fruit and poor food.
- **Quarantine and isolation of the sick** [`quarantine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/quarantine.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. In 1679 gatherings went on until July and closures came too late. The lazaretto lies outside the walls on the Als, among the suburbs burned on 13 July. Local: Pestlazarett St. Johannes in der Siechenals (run by the Bürgerspital); Bäckenhäusel on the Währinger Straße; Sorbait as Generalinquisitor in plague matters (1679). Elsewhere: Venice and Ragusa: permanent lazarettos and health magistracies.
- **Hospital hygiene and trained nursing** [`nursing_hospital_hygiene`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/nursing_hospital_hygiene.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Hospitals are houses of charity for the poor, old and sick, with beds shared. During the siege Bishop Kollonitsch sets up emergency hospitals in monasteries. Local: Bürgerspital (former convent of St. Clara); Barmherzige Brüder in the Leopoldstadt (lost to the Ottomans in mid-July); Leopold Karl von Kollonitsch.
- **Cholera and typhoid spread through drinking water** [`cholera_waterborne`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cholera_waterborne.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Cholera is unknown in Europe. The same reasoning applies to the rote Ruhr, which breaks out around 8 August and is not connected with wells or latrines.
- **Oral rehydration (water, salt and sugar)** [`oral_rehydration`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/oral_rehydration.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Ruhr patients get rhubarb purges, astringents, opiates and bleeding. Salt, honey and clean boiled water exist in the city; sugar is an apothecary's ware and dear. Local: apothecaries; Starhemberg, ill with dysentery 11–20 August.
- **Plague carried by rats and fleas (and by coughing)** [`plague_vectors`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/plague_vectors.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. The plague of 1679 is explained by corrupted air, infected goods and sin. Rats and fleas are not suspected. Infected bedding is burned or buried, which helps by accident. Local: Paul de Sorbait; Pestsäule vowed by Leopold I on the Graben (1679).
- **Typhus carried by body lice (delousing)** [`typhus_lice`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/typhus_lice.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Camp fever is known to imperial army physicians as the Hungarian disease (morbus Hungaricus) and blamed on air, water and food. Lice are ordinary. Epidemic follows the siege in autumn.
- **Malaria carried by mosquitoes (drainage, nets)** [`malaria_mosquito`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/malaria_mosquito.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Tertian and quartan fevers are common along the Danube wetlands and in Hungary and are blamed on marsh air. Avoiding marshes is the only defence.
- **Cinchona bark (quinine) against malaria** [`quinine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/quinine.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Jesuits' bark comes through the Society and Italian drug trade: dear, often adulterated, dosed too low. Galenists distrust it. None can be bought once the city is cut off. Local: Jesuit college and its apothecary; city apothecaries. Elsewhere: Rome: Jesuit distribution since the 1640s; London and Paris: Talbor's remedy, the recipe published in 1682.
- **Consumption (tuberculosis) is contagious** [`tuberculosis_control`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/tuberculosis_control.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Fracastoro's listing of phthisis among contagions is in print, but physicians treat consumption as an inherited constitution with catarrh falling on the lungs.
- **Parasitic worms (hookworm, roundworm, tapeworm, guinea worm)** [`parasitic_worms`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/parasitic_worms.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Worms are seen and treated with wormseed and bitter herbs, but held to arise from putrid humours in the gut. Itch mites and trichinae are unknown. Elsewhere: Florence: Redi, whose book on animals living inside animals appears in 1684.
- **Fresh food prevents scurvy (citrus, vitamin C)** [`scurvy_citrus`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scurvy_citrus.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Scharbock is a named disease of garrisons and winter; scurvy grass, cress and sauerkraut are the accepted remedies. Lemons come from Italy and are a luxury. Local: apothecaries (Löffelkraut preparations); noble and monastery orangeries.
- **Deficiency diseases (beriberi, rickets, pellagra, goitre, night blindness)** [`vitamins_deficiency`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/vitamins_deficiency.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Goitre and cretinism are familiar from the Alpine valleys of Styria and Carinthia and blamed on water. Rickets is in print (Glisson 1650). Nobody thinks a food can lack something.
- **Variolation (inoculation with smallpox matter)** [`variolation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/variolation.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Smallpox (Blattern) is endemic; it killed Leopold's elder brother Ferdinand IV in 1654. Giving it on purpose would be judged tempting God, and a death would be the inoculator's. Elsewhere: China: nasal insufflation; folk practice in parts of the Ottoman lands and Africa, not yet reported in Europe.
- **Smallpox vaccination with cowpox** [`smallpox_vaccination`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/smallpox_vaccination.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Cowpox would have to be found on a dairy herd and recognised, with no way to send to anyone for it.
- **Vaccines from weakened or killed germs** [`vaccines_attenuated`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/vaccines_attenuated.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept low
- **Antitoxin serum (passive immunisation)** [`antitoxin_serum`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/antitoxin_serum.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept low
- **Wound care (stop bleeding, clean, tie vessels, leave dirty wounds open)** [`wound_care`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wound_care.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Feldschere tie vessels and amputate after Paré, but probe shot wounds with fingers, close them early and welcome pus. The engineer Rimpler dies of an arm wound of 25 July. Local: regimental Feldschere; guild of Bader and Wundärzte; emergency hospitals in monasteries. Elsewhere: Halberstadt: Purmann, Der rechte und wahrhafftige Feldscher (1680); Ulm: Scultetus, Armamentarium chirurgicum (1655).
- **Antiseptics (strong spirit, chlorinated lime, carbolic acid, iodine)** [`antiseptics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/antiseptics.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Wine, vinegar, brandy and turpentine go on wounds by habit, not by rule. Against plague, rooms and letters are smoked with juniper and sulphur and washed with vinegar.
- **Sterilising instruments and dressings by heat** [`heat_sterilisation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/heat_sterilisation.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Instruments are wiped, lint (Charpie) is plucked from old linen by any hands. Boiling them would cost only firewood, scarce in the siege.
- **Safe childbirth (clean hands, patience, cord care, forceps)** [`childbirth_care`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/childbirth_care.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Births belong to sworn midwives; a surgeon is called only to extract a dead child with hooks. The forceps is a family secret in England. Elsewhere: London: Chamberlen family's forceps; Paris: Mauriceau's treatise (1668); Berlin: Justine Siegemund, court midwife.
- **First aid and resuscitation** [`first_aid_resuscitation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/first_aid_resuscitation.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. The drowned and suffocated are taken for dead. The wounded are carried from the bastions by comrades without any sorting by urgency.
- **Ether anaesthesia** [`ether_anaesthesia`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/ether_anaesthesia.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept medium. Apothecaries have oil of vitriol and spirit of wine, and Cordus's sweet oil of vitriol is in print. Nobody inhales it. Amputations are done fast, on brandy and opium.
- **Pain relief with opium and willow bark (laudanum, morphine, aspirin)** [`opium_analgesia`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/opium_analgesia.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Opium is in theriac and in laudanum pills at every apothecary, of uncertain strength; stocks are finite in the siege. Willow bark is not used against fever or pain. Elsewhere: London: Sydenham's liquid laudanum.
- **Blood groups and transfusion** [`blood_groups_transfusion`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/blood_groups_transfusion.md) — K2, use none, make very-hard, accept low. The lamb's-blood transfusions of the 1660s and the Paris ban are known from journals. Without blood groups any attempt is a lottery. Elsewhere: Purmann, army surgeon, tried lamb's blood on men 1668–1678 and gave it up.
- **Human anatomy from dissection** [`anatomy_dissection`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/anatomy_dissection.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Vesalian anatomy is taught from books; dissections at the university are rare. Ambitious physicians train at Padua, as Sorbait did (doctorate 1652). Local: Paul de Sorbait, professor of anatomy and practice since 1666. Elsewhere: Padua, Leiden, Paris, Bologna (Malpighi).
- **Circulation of the blood** [`blood_circulation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/blood_circulation.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. A student of Sorbait defended the circulation at Vienna in 1669. It is accepted in theory and changes nothing in practice: bleeding goes on. Local: Paul de Sorbait.
- **Physical diagnosis (percussion, stethoscope, thermometer, pulse count)** [`clinical_thermometer_stethoscope`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/clinical_thermometer_stethoscope.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Diagnosis is by pulse quality, urine glass and the patient's account. Sealed spirit thermometers exist as philosophical instruments without a fixed scale. Elsewhere: Florence: sealed spirit thermometers of the Accademia del Cimento; Padua: Santorio's printed methods.
- **Tooth decay and dental care** [`dental_care`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/dental_care.md) — K1, use wrong, make easy, accept medium. Toothache is blamed on the tooth worm and humours; teeth are pulled by barbers and market tooth-drawers. Sugar is a growing court fashion. Elsewhere: Delft: Leeuwenhoek's letter on animalcules in tooth scrapings, 17 September 1683.
